portion_doctrine: This portion is primarily video transcripts covering: (1) Google AI Studio for free web app building, (2) APPA tool for fast business app creation, (3) AI/automation opportunity identification using lean six sigma, (4) Claude/OpenClaw setup, security, and skill integration, (5) OpenClaw security hardening. Content is instructional/tactical with video timestamps. Boilerplate: repetitive UI navigation instructions, UI description text. Gold: specific frameworks, methodology names, tactical numbers, prompt patterns.
operating_rules: 3-step process for web app building: idea generation, build with AI Studio, deploy with Google Cloud
Identify AI automation opportunities: high volume of cases/tickets, rules-based process, measurable time/cost impact
Lean Six Sigma methodology: define problem, measure data (volume, rules, time per step, defect rates), analyze bottlenecks, improve
APPA tool workflow: create prompt, select capabilities (sales methodologies, marketing, backend integration), assign dummy data, test triggers, export
OpenClaw security audit: run daily scheduled audits, restrict tool policies to message-only mode, deny automation/runtime/FS groups
Tool access isolation: run tools in isolation to control outcomes and prevent bugs
Prompt injection defense: secure system prompts, gateway authentication, random port assignment, network isolation via Tailscale
named_methods: Lean Six Sigma (originating from 1950s Toyota production)
DMAIC framework (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control)
Quality assurance sampling (extract 1-10% of cases monthly to analyze AI response correctness)
numbers: 95% (failure rate for AI/automation projects in MIT study reference)
specific_tactics: Use Google AI Studio gallery for idea inspiration before building
Test prompts immediately after creation with sample queries (e.g. 'I hate working with you. Give me main starter prompt')
Iteratively refine prompts based on response quality
Re-execute with updated prompt in place
Map processes end-to-end before automation, identify specific steps consuming most time
Document customer service tickets over weeks/days to identify patterns (returns, pricing, feature usage, password reset)
Set OpenClaw task backlog: require human approval before execution, add hourly reminders (8am-11pm) for pending tasks
Use Claude Opus 4.5 or Gemini over ChatGPT for better outputs
Enable Chrome extension skill for local machine automation
Copy/paste security prompts rather than using terminal (reduces entry friction)
prompts: Example AI Studio test prompt: 'I hate working with you. Can you give me the main starter prompt?'
OpenClaw task management: 'Please can you enable the Chrome extension skill for me on my machine'
Backlog discipline prompt: 'Never execute ideas without my permission. Always add to backlog. Remind me every hour of pending tasks.'
tools: Google AI Studio (free web app builder)
OpenClaw (self-hosted Claude wrapper with security hardening)
gates: Permission gate: require human approval before executing AI-generated ideas
Prompt security gate: validate prompt structure before re-execution
Tool isolation gate: run tools in isolation to prevent major bugs or malicious outcomes
QA gate: monthly sampling of 1-10% of automated cases for human review
Access control gate: OpenClaw tool policy restrictive mode (message-only, deny automation/FS)
content_ideas: Free app building workflow using Google AI Studio (targeting developers on tight budgets)
APPA tool deep dive: rapid app prototyping in 2-3 minutes
AI opportunity identification: applying six sigma to automation decisions
OpenClaw security hardening: 10-step lockdown for self-hosted Claude
Process analysis framework: identifying high-impact automation targets
Lean six sigma ROI calculations for AI implementation
Claude Hub skills ecosystem: extending Claude with third-party integrations
contradictions: Content claims Google AI Studio and APPA are 'completely free' but both mention beta status, potential limitations, and errors ('some of it may work every now and again').
Security emphasis (OpenClaw hardening) contradicts ease-of-use messaging for general users (Claude with dangerous permissions).
Pro-AI automation stance (95% failure rate fixable) vs. acknowledge that many AI projects still fail despite best practices.
weird_gold: Whisper Flow tool mentioned casually for 'speeding up transcription review' but no explanation of how it works.
Random port assignment for OpenClaw to evade automated scans: clever obfuscation tactic, suggests active threat model.
APPA allows 'exporting' generated apps directly to individuals, suggesting serverless/instant deploy architecture, not typical of most web app builders.
Lean Six Sigma originated in 1950s Toyota: historical grounding adds credibility to methodology.
QA sampling recommendation (1-10% of cases) is industry standard but executed on AI output, raising question of variance/drift detection cadence.
